Which of the following statements are true about longshore drift?
Tick three answers.
AO1: Knowledge and understanding
•
Movement of material up and down the beach is repeated with each
wave.
•
The prevailing wind influences the direction of longshore drift movement.
•
Waves approach the coastline at an angle.
4 selected answers (maximum 2 marks)
5 selected answers (maximum 1 mark)
6 or more selected answers (0 marks)

SPECIMEN

Use Figure 1.7 and Table 1.4 to decide which coastal defence is the best.
Use data to justify your decision.
AO3: Evaluation and decision-making
Use Table A to mark candidate responses to this question.
Ideas such as:
Decision should be based upon and supported by evidence from Figure 1.7
and Table 1.4, e.g. best coastal defence are groynes.
Reference is made to advantages and disadvantages of each coastal
defence:
•
sea wall and/or rock armour protects coast from erosion the most (+3)
•
groynes only score +1 for coastal protection/does it stop wave erosion?
•
for attractiveness all score low: groynes +1, sea wall –1, rock armour –2
•
for access to the beach groynes score the highest +3, whereas sea wall
and rock armour both score –3
•
all score low for is it safe to walk on: groynes –3, sea wall –2, rock
armour –3.
Comparison between the positive and negative scores for the three
defences:
•
groynes score positively for four features and sea wall/rock armour score
positively for two features
•
groynes: positive scores for attractiveness, access to beach, protect
coast, stop wave erosion
•
sea wall and rock armour: positive scores for protect coast, stop wave
erosion.
Comparison between the total scores for the three defences:
e.g. only groynes have a positive score/groynes have highest score/total
score for groynes = +3, for sea wall = 0, for rock armour = –3.
Consideration of the different importance given to individual features of
each defence:
e.g. groynes score higher than the other methods/only positive score for
attractiveness and access to beach:
•
attractiveness: groynes = +1, sea wall = –1, rock armour = –2
•
access to beach: groynes = +3, sea wall = –3, rock armour = –3.
However, groynes score lower than the other methods for protects coast and
stops wave erosion:
•
protects coast: groynes = +1, sea wall = +3, rock armour = +2
•
stops wave erosion: groynes = +1, sea wall = +3, rock armour = +3.
Some evaluative comment as to which coastal defence is best with justification.
All valid material must be credited.

Define the following terms.
AO1 Knowledge and understanding
•
economic migrant – a person who travels from one country or area
to another in order to improve their standard of living/for jobs/for more
money.
•
refugee – a person who leaves their country of origin because of fear or
persecution and asks for permission to stay in a different country.
2 × 1 mark

Explain what is meant by push and pull factors. Do not give examples.
AO1 Knowledge and understanding
•
Push factors: reasons/negative factors which make/encourage people to
leave/go away from an area/country/emigrate.
•
Pull factors: reasons/positive factors which attract/make people want to
come to an area/country/immigrate.
2 × 1 mark

Use the data in Table 2.3 to explain to what extent was the migrants’
move to Rome a success for the migrants.
Include statistics from Table 2.3 to justify your answer.
AO3: Evaluation and decision-making
Use Table A to mark candidate responses to this question.
Don’t agree because:
•
(many) migrants regretted their decision to move to Rome
•
migrants said that problems were greater than benefits, e.g. 420 answers
for problems and 280 answers for benefits
•
the main problems identified was high cost of living which was higher
scoring than the main benefit of opportunity to work, e.g. high cost of
living = 92 answers and opportunity to work = 67 answers
•
the three main problems were all higher scoring than the main benefit,
e.g. 92, 74, 69 answers compared with 67 answers
•
more problems were identified than benefits, e.g. 8 problems and
6 benefits.
Agree/partially agree it was a success because:
•
migrants can get jobs (67 out of 100)
•
children can go to school (64 out of 100)
•
there is good healthcare (53 out of 100).
Decision should be made based on and supported by evidence in Table 2.3.
Reference is made to benefits and problems identified in Table 2.3.
Comparison between the number of benefits and problems in Table 2.3.
Comparison between the number of answers identifying problems and
benefits in total in Table 2.3.
Consideration of the different importance given to individual benefits and
problems identified in Table 2.3.
Overall conclusion e.g. disagree because there are more problems identified
than benefits etc.
All valid material must be credited.
